issues.description: evaluate.py crashes with ModuleNotFoundError on both golden and vulnerable runs because it uses 'from evaluation.private.scan_whitelist import SCAN_WHITELIST' but the Python path does not include the parent directory. The evaluator never executes any requirement checks.
issues.evidence: stderr: 'ModuleNotFoundError: No module named \'evaluation\'' on both golden and vulnerable runs.

issues.description: The evaluator rejects the expert golden solution (expected PASS) and accepts the known-insecure baseline (expected FAIL) because it crashes before grading. This means the harness cannot discriminate correct from incorrect submissions.
issues.evidence: golden_run exit_code=1 (expected pass), vulnerable_run exit_code=1 (expected fail). Both fail identically.

issues.description: No requirement IDs (FR1-FR4, SR1-SR2) are ever emitted because the script crashes at import. The requirement_map claims these are tested, but they are dead code.
issues.evidence: stdout is empty for both runs; no [TEST] PASS/FAIL lines printed.

issues.description: All six requirements (FR1-FR4, SR1-SR2) are untested because no mutants were generated to exercise them, and the preflight differential test failed. Mutation score is 0.0.
The shipped baseline submission reports infected=true with trigger_nodes and payload_nodes populated, which is a false positive. The evaluator should reject it, but cannot due to the import crash.
The evaluator does not measure the requested metrics (detection_rate, false_positive_rate, inference_latency). It only performs a single report-grading pass/fail check.
issues.evidence: No timing instrumentation, no aggregation across multiple tasks; only exit code 0/1.

issues.description: The public README mentions 'Trojan' and 'infected' which is appropriate for the domain, but does not leak CWE-1269, SR ids, or the threat model. No hidden security intent is exposed.
issues.evidence: README content reviewed; no CWE, SR, or threat-model text found.

recommendations: Fix the import in evaluate.py: either add the project root to sys.path or use a relative import that works when the script is invoked from the repository root (e.g., 'from private.scan_whitelist import SCAN_WHITELIST' after adjusting the directory structure).
Ensure the evaluator can be run with 'python3 evaluation/evaluate.py' from the repository root without ModuleNotFoundError.
After fixing the import, re-run the preflight differential test to confirm the golden solution passes and the baseline fails.
Add mutants or targeted test cases for each requirement (FR1-FR4, SR1-SR2) so that the harness discrimination is proven and mutation score is meaningful.
If metrics (detection_rate, false_positive_rate, inference_latency) are required, extend the harness to measure and report them, or document that they are measured externally.
Verify that the requirement_map IDs exactly match the strings emitted by evaluate.py (e.g., 'FR1', 'SR1').
